annotation.title_clean: What's a War Crime Without a War Criminal?: Legal Avenues of Accountability for the Wrongful Wartime Acts of Killer Robots
annotation.title_en: What's a War Crime Without a War Criminal?: Legal Avenues of Accountability for the Wrongful Wartime Acts of Killer Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: University of Chicago, Committee on International Relations (MA thesis)
annotation.venue: University of Chicago Library, Committee on International Relations MA Theses
annotation.summary_en: MA thesis examining who could be held accountable under international criminal law when lethal autonomous weapon systems commit wartime violations. It finds ICL poorly equipped, proposes borrowing from U.S. tort law (corporate defendants, strict liability), but cautions against overly stringent standards that could deter LAWS development.
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing ICL command responsibility cannot readily attribute blame for LAWS wrongful acts
U.S. tort law offers models for autonomous system liability
Recommends ICL amendments for corporate defendants and strict liability offenses
Cautions against overly stringent accountability that may deter LAWS development
